text: Given a valid Umbrella API key/secret pair, When cisco_umbrella_list_api_keys is called, Then it returns the account's API key list (id, label, scope, status) and no key contains a secret field
evidence: uv run pytest -q tests/test_tools.py::test_list_api_keys_returns_metadata_without_secret -> 1 passed (dev worktree, 2026-10-30, re-run after review round 1 fixes)

text: Given a real Managed Provider Umbrella account, When cisco_umbrella_list_api_keys is called end to end, Then the live response is a non-empty array and no item contains a secret field
steps: Set UMBRELLA_API_KEY/UMBRELLA_KEY_SECRET to a real MSPbots test account (needs a real vendor account)
Call cisco_umbrella_list_api_keys via the local stdio server
expect: Non-empty array of key objects (id, label/keyType, scope, status); grep the raw response for any secret-like field and confirm none is present
notes: needs a real vendor account; not executed during design or dev (no account available in either pass, per mcp-track.md 2.5 this does not block 6b). Dev also tried to re-confirm the endpoint's exact shape/pagination against Cisco's public docs and could not: docs.umbrella.com/umbrella-api/reference/getadminapikeys 301-redirects to a generic securitydocs.cisco.com landing page as of 2026-10-30 (see README Known Gaps). Flagged for post-release verification against a real account.

text: Given organization_id=A, When cisco_umbrella_list_destination_lists is called, Then the request is scoped via X-Umbrella-OrgId at token-mint time, matching the existing reports.py pattern
evidence: uv run pytest -q tests/test_tools.py::test_list_destination_lists_is_scoped_by_organization_id -> 1 passed (dev worktree, 2026-10-30, re-run after review round 1 fixes; tool unchanged in behavior for this call shape, destination_list_id omitted)

text: Given two different managed customers (org A, org B) on a real Managed Provider account, When cisco_umbrella_list_destination_lists is called once per org, Then the two responses are disjoint (no cross-tenant data)
steps: Resolve two organization_id values via cisco_umbrella_list_customers (needs a real vendor account with 2+ managed customers)
Call cisco_umbrella_list_destination_lists with org A's id
Call cisco_umbrella_list_destination_lists with org B's id
expect: The two destination-list responses are disjoint (different ids/names), proving org A's call never leaks org B's policy data and vice versa
notes: needs a real vendor account with at least 2 managed customers; mirrors the existing org-scope test already in this repo. Not executed during design or dev (no account available in either pass, per mcp-track.md 2.5 this does not block 6b). The underlying org-scoping mechanism itself (X-Umbrella-OrgId applied at token-mint time, never on the business request) is unchanged code, reused verbatim from the already-live-verified reports.py path — see test_org_scope_is_applied_at_token_mint_not_on_the_business_request — so this gap is specifically about the Policies v2 endpoint's live response shape, not the scoping mechanism.

text: Given organization_id=A, When cisco_umbrella_list_application_lists and cisco_umbrella_get_application_usage are called, Then both return that customer's application-list/usage data via GET /policies/v2/applicationLists and GET /policies/v2/applications/usage

text: Given any domain name, When cisco_umbrella_get_domain_risk_score and cisco_umbrella_get_domain_whois are called, Then each returns the expected shape (numeric risk score; WHOIS record with registrant/registrar/nameServers)

Re-run after review round 1: both are now cisco_umbrella_get_domain_intel(domain, aspect="risk_score"|"whois") per the review's must-fix (see PRD-21226-review.md Round 1 Fixes); same two capabilities, same test asserts the same two response shapes.

text: Given a gateway-mode request missing the X-Umbrella-Api-Key/X-Umbrella-Key-Secret headers, When any of the 8 new tools is called, Then it returns the same not_configured structured error the existing 14 tools return
evidence: uv run pytest -q tests/test_tools.py::test_new_tools_return_not_configured_without_gateway_headers -> 1 passed (dev worktree, 2026-10-30, re-run after review round 1 fixes; call list updated to the consolidated tool names/params but still covers all 8 capability points, now surfaced through 6 tool names). Also confirmed over the real HTTP wire: POST /mcp with no X-Umbrella-* headers against a local server (uv run cisco-umbrella-mcp, MCP_TRANSPORT=http AUTH_MODE=gateway) returned 401, and GET /health returned 200 throughout.

text: Given an upstream 401/403/404/429/5xx response from any new endpoint, When the corresponding tool is called, Then it returns the same structured error_envelope with the same status-to-code mapping as the existing tools (no stack trace, no raw HTML)
evidence: uv run pytest -q tests/test_tools.py::test_new_tools_map_upstream_errors_to_envelope -> 1 passed (dev worktree, 2026-10-30, re-run after review round 1 fixes; cases updated to call cisco_umbrella_get_domain_intel with aspect=risk_score/whois instead of the two retired tool names). Also confirmed live: calling cisco_umbrella_get_domain_intel(aspect="risk_score") over the real HTTP wire with placeholder (fake) credentials produced a genuine upstream 401 from api.umbrella.com, mapped to {"error":{"code":"unauthorized","message":"Unauthorized","retryable":false}} with no stack trace.

text: Given organization_id=A and destination_list_id=dl1, When cisco_umbrella_list_destination_lists is called, Then it returns the domains/URLs inside that one list (via GET /policies/v2/destinationlists/{id}/destinations) instead of the list of lists

Added by dev to cover the optional-param branch introduced by the review round 1 consolidation of cisco_umbrella_get_destination_list_destinations into cisco_umbrella_list_destination_lists (see PRD-21226-review.md Round 1 Fixes); not a design-defined AC per se, but AC2's own text already anticipated this exact shape ("or, given a destination_list_id, the destinations inside one list").
